Attention: Océane Lefèvre, Chief Executive Officer

Re: Side Letter — Series B Preferred Stock Financing

Dear Ms. Lefèvre:

Reference is made to that certain Series B Preferred Stock Purchase Agreement of even date herewith (the "Purchase Agreement") among Thalassa Marine Robotics, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "Company"), Kestrel Deepwater Partners III, L.P. ("Kestrel"), and the other investors named in it. Capitalized terms used and not defined in this letter have the meanings given to them in the Purchase Agreement or, if not defined there, in the Amended and Restated Investors' Rights Agreement of even date (the "IRA").

In consideration of Kestrel's purchase of Series B Preferred Stock, and as a condition to the Closing, the Company agrees with Kestrel as follows. This letter is binding on the Company and Kestrel and is enforceable as an agreement separate from, and in addition to, the Purchase Agreement.

1. Board Observer.

For so long as Kestrel and its affiliates continue to hold at least fifty percent (50%) of the shares of Series B Preferred Stock purchased by Kestrel at the Closing, Kestrel may designate one representative to attend all meetings of the Board of Directors and of each committee in a non-voting observer capacity. The Company shall give the observer the same notice and the same materials it gives the directors, at the same time. The Company may exclude the observer from any portion of a meeting, and withhold any material, if the Board determines in good faith that exclusion is reasonably necessary to preserve the attorney-client privilege or to avoid a conflict of interest, and shall tell the observer that it has done so. The observer shall enter into a confidentiality agreement in the form the Company reasonably requests before attending any meeting.

2. Information Rights Without a Minimum Holding.

Notwithstanding the Major Investor threshold in Section 3 of the IRA, Kestrel is entitled to the information rights described in that Section for so long as it holds any shares of Series B Preferred Stock.

3. Pro Rata Rights in a Deemed Liquidation Event.

If the Board approves a Deemed Liquidation Event in which the consideration includes securities of the acquiror, Kestrel is entitled to receive the same form and mix of consideration, and the same per-share value, as the holder receiving the most favorable treatment among the holders of Series B Preferred Stock.

4. Most Favored Nation.

If the Company grants to any other purchaser of Series B Preferred Stock a right that is more favorable to that purchaser than the corresponding right granted to Kestrel in this letter or in the Definitive Agreements, the Company shall promptly notify Kestrel and, at Kestrel's election, extend the same right to Kestrel. This Section does not apply to a right granted to a strategic investor in connection with a commercial agreement, or to a right conditioned on an investment amount larger than Kestrel's.

5. Regulatory and Tax Covenants.

The Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to determine, within forty-five (45) days after the end of each fiscal year, whether it was a "passive foreign investment company" within the meaning of Section 1297 of the Internal Revenue Code, and shall provide Kestrel with the information reasonably necessary for Kestrel to make a qualified electing fund election if it was. The Company shall also make a reasonable determination annually as to whether its stock constitutes a "United States real property interest" and shall furnish the certification described in Treasury Regulation § 1.897-2(h) on request.

6. Confidentiality.

Kestrel shall keep confidential all non-public information it receives under this letter, subject to the exceptions and permitted disclosures in Section 3.5 of the IRA, which apply to this letter as if set forth here.

7. Termination.

Sections 1 through 5 terminate on the earlier of (a) the closing of a firm-commitment underwritten public offering by the Company, and (b) the closing of a Deemed Liquidation Event. Section 6 survives indefinitely. If the Purchase Agreement is terminated before the Closing, this letter terminates at the same time and is of no further force or effect.

8. No Amendment to the Definitive Agreements.

Nothing in this letter amends, waives, or supersedes any provision of the Purchase Agreement, the IRA, or any other Definitive Agreement. In the event of a conflict between this letter and a Definitive Agreement, this letter governs as between the Company and Kestrel only, and the Definitive Agreement governs as to every other party.

9. Assignment.

Kestrel may assign its rights under this letter to an affiliate to which it transfers shares of Series B Preferred Stock. The Company may not assign this letter without Kestrel's prior written consent, except to a successor in a Deemed Liquidation Event that assumes this letter in writing.

10. Governing Law; Counterparts.

This letter is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. It may be executed in counterparts and amended only in a writing signed by the Company and Kestrel.

Please confirm the Company's agreement by countersigning below.

Very truly yours,

KESTREL DEEPWATER PARTNERS III, L.P.
